title: Reservation decision proto-playbook — 1:1 prep & follow-ups
text:
Goal: rapid pre-brief for weekly 1:1 with Kenji (pool ops) + follow-ups to drive a clear reservation decision for Q2 commit window. Keep this as a compact playbook we can run through in <15m and then hand off to finance + SRE.

Context:
- We're seeing seasonal uptick in inference jobs for vision rerank (late-season retail customers) and a steady rise in embedding usage from two PLG customers.
- Current dedicated pool: 40xA100 equiv (mixed q8/amp); committed utilization target historically 70%.
- Forecast signals: expected +20% q/q demand for the next three months on tail of new product rollout. Burst capacity is limited (max +12 GPUs spot-like).

Core question for the meeting:
- Do we increase committed capacity in the dedicated pool now, and by how much, vs leaning on autoscale/burst? Which combination minimizes spend while keeping SLO risk < 3% for p95 latency?

Decision criteria (what must be true to commit):
1) Projected committed utilization >= 65% over 3-month rolling horizon.
2) Incremental committed cost / avoided on-demand cost < 0.6 (simple payback threshold).
3) No single customer onboarding increases p95 failure risk above 1.5x current baseline.
4) Finance sign-off on headroom buffer (0–12 GPUs) within weekly budget.

Data to pull before the call (explicit queries):
- 7/14/30-day token-per-model and per-customer demand curves (agg by hour-of-day).
- Historical burst frequency: count of bursts >4 GPUs and >12 GPUs over last 90 days.
- Queue wait time distribution for dedicated routes (p50/p95/p99) for last 30 days.
- Cost per-token on committed vs burst/ondemand for the candidate SKU mix (quantized/float mixes).

Hypotheses to test in the meeting (quick statements):
- H1: 8–12 additional committed A100-equiv buys will keep us within cost budgets and reduce p95 latency regressions during peak windows.
- H2: If burst + autoscale config is tuned (lower batch cap, prioritized prompt lanes) we can defer commit for one quarter with <5% SLA risk.
- H3: The new PLG cohort will push embedding tail beyond 80% utilization within 6 weeks if we do not increase capacity.

Back-of-envelope economics (rough numbers to sanity-check in meeting):
- Current committed cost: $X/month for 40 GPUs (replace with numbers in live sheet). Ballpark: $200k/mo (example) -> per-GPU ~5k/mo.
- On-demand/blended burst cost ~2.1x committed.
- If we add 10 GPUs committed: delta cost ~= $50k/mo. If avoids >24k/mo extra burst spend -> ratio 0.48 -> meets threshold.

Premortem: If we commit wrong, what happens?
- Overcommit: idle spend increases, pressure on finance, harder to sell to CRO; mitigations: ability to scale down at renewal, add soft-burst pricing tiers.
- Undercommit: p95 spikes, some customers will throttle or leave; mitigations: emergency burst credit, priority routing to hosted pool, temporary rate limits with customer SRE notice.
- Unexpected failure modes: driver/infra churn when new SKU mix is introduced. Ask release-eng to schedule smoke testing on canary subset.

Meeting agenda (8–12 min):
1) 1 min: quick objective + Yes/No framing
2) 3 min: show two forecast scenarios (conservative; upside) + utilization curves
3) 2 min: economics summary (commit delta vs expected burst cost)
4) 2 min: risk/premortem and ops readiness
5) 2 min: decision + owners + next steps

Proposed immediate next steps (post-decision follow-ups):
- If commit=yes: create JIRA ticket to request procurement (owner: Sophie) — include SKU mix, preferred start date, rollback windows. Due: 48h.
- If commit=no: schedule autoscale tuning spike with SRE (owner: Ethan) to implement throttle/QoS and measure effect for 3 weeks. Due: config pushed in 5 business days.
- Cross-cutting: finance to prepare budget amendment and burn projection for exec sign-off (owner: Kenji). Due: EOW.
- Release-engineering smoke test: spin 4 test instances with new quantization/driver profile and run 24h soak. Owner: release-eng contact (linked in artifacts). Due: 7 days.

Follow-up action item table (to drop into JIRA quickly):
- SOP-001: procurement ticket w/ SKU + start/end dates (Sophie) — due 2 days
- SOP-002: autoscale QoS change: lower max-batch, prioritized lanes (Ethan) — due 5 days
- SOP-003: finance budget delta + sign-off memo (Kenji) — due 5 days
- SOP-004: canary smoke test + incident playbook (release-eng) — due 7 days

Open questions to raise live:
- What is the acceptable payback ratio from finance (is 0.6 firm or negotiable)?
- Can we get a one-time vendor credit for first-month headroom if we sign within quarter?
- Are there upcoming client onboarding dates that should accelerate the timeline?

Notes-to-self (quick reminders):
- Keep the ask binary in the meeting: "increase committed by N GPUs" vs "defer and tune autoscale".
- Bring the hourly utilization chart — nothing else unless asked.
- If Kenji pushes for more conservative number, propose a split: commit 6 now + option to convert 4 after 30 days if utilization >72%.

Tone for the 1:1: pragmatic, numbers-first, show tradeoffs candidly. Ask for the simplest path that preserves p95 SLO while minimizing capex. Close with a concrete owner and timeline.

End of doc: will paste actionable items into JIRA immediately after call and ping finance slack channel with the budget delta.
